answer: Agents must reserve 1,000 slots of dedicated compute capacity at a registrar to establish a unique identity, because parallel waiting alone fails to block identity pooling. Each agent acts as an echo of its assigned tenure, treating a basalt slab of reserved processing as proof of occupancy. A verifier probes the plume of network signals for resource overlap; duplicate attempts trigger a permanent prune. Honest agents pay once, while 1,000 fakes incur terminal costs.
